title: Affine algebra class maps preserve evaluation and open restriction
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring, let $C$ be a commutative $B$-algebra whose degree-zero complex $C[0]$ is pseudo-coherent over $B$ [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], and let $T\in D(B)$ satisfy $H^i(T)=0$ for all $i<t$ for some integer $t$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $F_B(P)=\widetilde P$ for the affine derived realization on $Z=\operatorname{Spec}B$ [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence]. Use derived tensor computed by K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex], and write $\mathsf H_B=R\operatorname{Hom}_B(C[0],T)$, with module derived Hom interpreted as [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site of $B$. There is a canonical isomorphism $\gamma_{C,T}:F_B(\mathsf H_B)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_Z(F_B(C[0]),F_B(T))$ in $D(\mathcal O_Z)$, natural in the first argument as a derived $B$-module and in $T$ [def-pc-derived-category]. It is normalized by evaluation: after the canonical isomorphism $F_B(P\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}Q)\cong F_B(P)\otimes_{\mathcal O_Z}^{\mathbf L}F_B(Q)$, the composite of $\gamma_{C,T}\otimes1$ with sheaf evaluation equals $F_B$ of module evaluation. For every $\xi:C[0]\to T$, define $m_\xi:C[0]\to\mathsf H_B$ as the transpose of $C[0]\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C[0]\xrightarrow{\mu_C}C[0]\xrightarrow{\xi}T$, where $\mu_C$ is induced by ordinary algebra multiplication; define $m_{F_B\xi}$ by the same transpose on sheaves [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then $\gamma_{C,T}\circ F_B(m_\xi)=m_{F_B\xi}$. These comparisons commute with all $B$-scalar endomorphisms and with precomposition by multiplication by every $c\in C$. For every ring map $\varphi:B\to D$ inducing an affine open immersion $j:\operatorname{Spec}D\hookrightarrow Z$, put $C_D=D\otimes_B C$, $T_D=D\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}T$, and $\xi_D=D\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}\xi$, identifying $D\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C[0]$ with $C_D[0]$. There are canonical natural restriction isomorphisms $j^*F_B(P)\cong F_D(D\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}P)$, compatible with derived tensor, and the evaluation-defined map $\lambda:D\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}\mathsf H_B\to R\operatorname{Hom}_D(C_D[0],T_D)$ is invertible. Under these isomorphisms and open restriction of derived internal Hom, $j^*\gamma_{C,T}$ equals $\gamma_{C_D,T_D}\circ F_D(\lambda)$, and $\lambda\circ(D\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}m_\xi)=m_{\xi_D}$. Here the tensor and evaluation comparisons are the ones induced by ordinary extension of scalars on K-flat representatives, rather than unspecified isomorphisms. The comparison diagrams commute also under successive affine-open restrictions.

proof.text: Fix the tensor comparison $\alpha_{P,Q}:F_B(P)\otimes^{\mathbf L}F_B(Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_B(P\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q)$ as follows. Take K-flat resolutions of both module complexes; their associated sheaf complexes are K-flat, and the total-tensor tilde comparison gives $\alpha$. Normalize the ordinary tensor comparison by $\tau(p)\otimes\tau(q)\mapsto\tau(p\otimes q)$. The cited affine derived tensor lemma supplies the resulting natural derived isomorphism. This is the comparison computed by extension of scalars, not a new choice of tensor structure. The ringed-site tensor-Hom adjunction supplies evaluation and its bijective transpose, both for the one-object ringed site of $B$ and for the Zariski ringed site of $Z$. Its K-flat uncurrying normalization is precisely evaluation on these representatives. Write $H(E,T)=R\operatorname{Hom}_B(E,T)$ and $\mathcal H(F_BE,F_BT)=R\mathcal Hom_Z(F_BE,F_BT)$.

proof.text:
For any $E,T\in D(B)$ define $\gamma_{E,T}:F_BH(E,T)\to\mathcal H(F_BE,F_BT)$ to be the sheaf tensor-Hom transpose of $F_B(\mathrm{ev}_{E,T})\circ\alpha_{H(E,T),E}$. Thus, by the inverse-transpose identity,
$$\mathrm{ev}_{F_BE,F_BT}\circ(\gamma_{E,T}\otimes1)=F_B(\mathrm{ev}_{E,T})\circ\alpha_{H(E,T),E}.$$
This constructs a specified comparison even before asserting invertibility. In particular it gives exactly the evaluation normalization of the item when $E=C[0]$.

proof.text:
Suppose $E$ is pseudo-coherent and $T$ is bounded below. The pseudo-coherent definition supplies a bounded-above finite free representative of $E$, hence a finite projective representative as required by the affine Hom lemma. That lemma puts $J=\mathcal H(F_BE,F_BT)$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$. For every $V\in D(B)$ there are natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(F_BV,F_BH(E,T))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(V,H(E,T))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(V\otimes^{\mathbf L}E,T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_BV\otimes^{\mathbf L}F_BE,F_BT)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_BV,J).$$
Here the first and third bijections use full faithfulness of the affine equivalence and $\alpha$, and the others are the two tensor-Hom adjunctions. By Step 2 this composite sends $h$ to $\gamma_{E,T}\circ h$. Choose $W$ and $v:F_BW\xrightarrow{\sim}J$ using essential surjectivity onto quasi-coherent objects. Surjectivity at $W$ gives $h:F_BW\to F_BH(E,T)$ with $\gamma h=v$, so $k=hv^{-1}$ is a right inverse to $\gamma$. Injectivity at $V=H(E,T)$ applied to $\gamma(k\gamma)=\gamma$ gives $k\gamma=1$. Thus $\gamma_{E,T}$ is invertible. This argument uses only the existing lemma's quasi-coherence conclusion, not an unspecified isomorphism as if it already preserved evaluation.

For $a:E'\to E$ and $b:T\to T'$, take inverse transposes of $\gamma_{E',T'}F_BH(a,b)$ and $\mathcal H(F_Ba,F_Bb)\gamma_{E,T}$. Naturality of evaluation and $\alpha$ makes both equal to
$$F_B(b\circ\mathrm{ev}_{E,T}\circ(1\otimes a))\circ\alpha_{H(E,T),E'}.$$
Injectivity of transposition proves naturality for actual derived morphisms in both variables. This argument needs no chain representative of $a$ or $b$. Specialize to $a$ equal to multiplication by $c\in C$ on $C[0]$ to obtain the precomposition square. Specialize to scalar multiplication on either input for every $b_0\in B$ to obtain all stated $B$-scalar squares; the comparisons are also morphisms of $\mathcal O_Z$-modules and so are $B$-linear.

proof.text: Put $E=C[0]$ and $q=\xi\circ\mu_C:E\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}E\to T$. By definition $\mathrm{ev}_{E,T}\circ(m_\xi\otimes1)=q$. The inverse transpose of $\gamma_{E,T}F_B(m_\xi)$ is consequently $F_B(q)\circ\alpha_{E,E}$. On K-flat resolutions mapping to $C[0]$, multiplication is represented by $p\otimes q'\mapsto\overline p\,\overline {q'}$ followed by $\xi$; termwise tilde and the normalized ordinary tensor map give the same sheaf multiplication. Thus $F_B(q)\alpha_{E,E}=F_B(\xi)\circ\mu_{F_BE}$. This is the inverse transpose defining $m_{F_B\xi}$, so injectivity of transposition gives $\gamma_{C,T}F_B(m_\xi)=m_{F_B\xi}$.

proof.text: For the given affine open immersion $j$, its local-ring maps are isomorphisms by the definition of open immersion. An isomorphism of rings is flat because its scalar-extension functor is the identity up to that isomorphism. The definition of flat morphism and the affine flatness criterion therefore show that $D$ is flat over $B$. Put $L=D\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}-$; the K-flat construction of derived change of rings and exactness of $D\otimes_B-$ identify $L$ with ordinary extension on complexes. Indeed tensoring preserves the cycle-boundary short exact sequences, hence commutes with cohomology and preserves quasi-isomorphisms. It follows that $LC[0]=C_D[0]$ and $H^i(LT)=D\otimes_B H^i(T)=0$ for $i<t$. Tensor a bounded-above finite free representative of $C[0]$ with $D$: its terms remain finite free, and exactness preserves the representative quasi-isomorphism, so $C_D[0]$ is pseudo-coherent over $D$. Thus Step 3 applies over $D$, with no Noetherian or perfectness assumption.

proof.text: Let $\rho_P:j^*F_BP\xrightarrow{\sim}F_DLP$ be the affine derived pullback comparison. Use its ordinary normalization from the tilde-pullback lemma: the pullback of $\tau(p)$ corresponds to $\tau(1\otimes p)$. It is natural in $P$. On K-flat representatives the tensor square for $\rho$ sends a pure tensor to the same element $d_1d_2\otimes(p\otimes q)$ by either path; the balancing relation proves equality, and the total-complex differential is preserved. These representative comparisons descend to the stated tensor-compatible restriction isomorphisms. Let $\kappa:j^*\mathcal H(F_BE,F_BT)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H(j^*F_BE,j^*F_BT)$ be the inverse of the open internal-Hom comparison. It preserves evaluation: restrict a K-injective representative of the second input (still K-injective), and the ordinary Hom-complex restriction isomorphism sends a family of maps to its restriction. Both resulting evaluation maps send $h\otimes p$ to $h(p)$, with the same total-complex degrees. Thus the derived square commutes by the representative normalization of the closed adjunction. This verifies the evaluation property rather than assuming that an arbitrary internal-Hom isomorphism has it.

proof.text: Write $H=H(E,T)$ and define $\lambda:LH\to H_D(LE,LT)$ by transposing $L(\mathrm{ev}_{E,T})$ after the extension-of-scalars tensor comparison. The latter is the map $ (d\otimes x)\otimes(e\otimes y)\mapsto de\otimes(x\otimes y)$ on K-flat representatives. Compare the two maps from $F_DLH$ to $\mathcal H(F_DLE,F_DLT)$ obtained (a) from $j^*\gamma_{E,T}$ via $\rho$ and $\kappa$, and (b) as $\gamma_{LE,LT}\circ F_D\lambda$. Their inverse transposes are equal: for (a), apply $j^*$ to the evaluation equation of Step 2, then the evaluation and tensor squares of Step 7; the result is $F_DL(\mathrm{ev}_{E,T})$ with the scalar-extension and affine tensor comparisons inserted. For (b), Step 2 over $D$ and the defining evaluation equation for $\lambda$ give exactly that same composite. Injectivity of sheaf transposition proves the asserted equality $j^*\gamma_{C,T}=\gamma_{C_D,T_D}\circ F_D\lambda$ under the displayed identifications.

proof.text: By Step 3 over $B$ and $D$, Step 6, and invertibility of $\rho$ and $\kappa$, the equality of Step 8 expresses $F_D\lambda$ as a composite of isomorphisms. Full faithfulness of $F_D$ lifts its inverse to an inverse of $\lambda$; faithfulness verifies both inverse identities. This proves invertibility of the specified map $\lambda$, rather than merely existence of some scalar-extension isomorphism. Finally the inverse transpose of $\lambda\circ Lm_\xi$ is $L(\xi\circ\mu_C)$ under the tensor comparison, by the defining equations of $\lambda$ and $m_\xi$. The scalar-extension formula gives the multiplication $(d\otimes c)(e\otimes c')=de\otimes cc'$ of $C_D$, so this inverse transpose is $\xi_D\circ\mu_{C_D}$. It defines $m_{\xi_D}$, and injectivity of module transposition proves $\lambda\circ Lm_\xi=m_{\xi_D}$.

proof.text: For successive affine open restrictions $B\to D\to D'$, identify repeated derived extension and repeated derived pullback with their composites by the canonical composition maps. On representative tensors the two extension identifications both send $e\otimes(d\otimes p)$ to $e\varphi'(d)\otimes p$; associativity of multiplication proves the equality also on tensor products. Restriction of ordinary Hom families is literally successive restriction, so its evaluation equation is also the composite equation. Consequently the successive $\rho$ identifications agree, compatibly with the associative derived-pullback composition isomorphisms. The two resulting maps $D'\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}H\to H_{D'}(D'\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}E,D'\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}T)$ have the identical inverse transpose, namely extension of the original evaluation. They are equal by injectivity. The same argument with $\xi\mu_C$ proves coherence for the multiplication class maps, and Step 8 then proves coherence for $\gamma$. Identity restrictions are the same calculation with the unit element. This proves every requested successive-restriction diagram.
